structured_output.summary:
I found no newer public CIFAR-100 result. The best published one is still futurebiohackers at 75.29% in 8.11 s, which the loop has already beaten at 5.2 s, and the only official baseline is ResNet9 at 59.3 s. So the useful outside evidence comes from CIFAR-10 speedruns and Muon papers. In rough order of usefulness:

1. **Batch size could vary with resolution (no hypothesis covers this yet).** fast.ai's 18-minute ImageNet run used larger batches during its low-resolution phase. E038 found per-step costs are larger in our 16/24 px phases. A schedule with bs about 3072 at 16/24 px and 1024–1536 at 32 px therefore looks promising. One caution: OLMo results show the critical batch size is near zero at the start of training and grows, so large batches early may cost more accuracy than E022 suggests.
2. **Cheap Muon tweaks from the hiverge record (bs 1536, Muon lr 0.205, momentum 0.655).** It keeps the Muon momentum buffer in fp16, which cuts the memory traffic E035 identified as the remaining cost. It schedules the renormalization target norm from 0.50 down to 0.079. It also freezes the BN affine weights, uses BN eps 1e-12, and trains the whitening bias only for the first 20% of steps. Its other settings (label smoothing 0.09, SiLU, colour jitter, linear decay to 0) were already tested here and lost.
3. **Warmup length is untested.** An agent-driven airbench96 run regained its accuracy margin after shortening the schedule by repairing the warmup, giving a 4.6% saving overall.
4. **Weak or negative leads.** Turbo-Muon AOL preconditioning: −0.8% time on CIFAR-10. Drop-Muon / FreezeOut, i.e. skipping backward passes for early layers: no gain for VGG-like nets. Critical-damping momentum schedules: cost 1.7 pp on CIFAR-100. MUD and NorMuon have only language-model results.
5. **Fable/fulcrum CIFAR-10 record (1.828 s).** It agrees with our results: CUDA graphs and optimizer fusion were neutral or slightly worse than plain torch.compile, and global max pooling is what makes low-resolution training work. Unlike our measurements, Fable kept its cheap phase at 24 px or above (24→28→32).

findings.claim: The hiverge CIFAR-10 record (1.98 s on A100) uses bs 1536, Muon lr 0.205, momentum 0.655, Nesterov and 3 NS iterations (a=3.4576, b=-4.7391, c=2.0843). It stores the Muon momentum buffer in torch.half, renormalizes every 4 steps (adaptive), and schedules the renorm target magnitude from 0.5012 to 0.0786 over training. BN affine weights are frozen, BN eps is 1e-12 and BN momentum is 0.5566. The whitening bias trains only for the first 20% of steps. wd = 1.04e-6*bs on both optimizers, the LR decays linearly to 0, label smoothing is 0.09, the activation is SiLU, and there is brightness/contrast jitter.
findings.relevance: Our E038 tip already matches the bs (1536) and the renorm cadence. Not yet tried: an fp16 momentum buffer, which cuts Muon memory traffic; E035 found that traffic plus NS matmuls is the remaining ~1 ms/step. Also untried: the scheduled renorm target norm, frozen BN affine weights, and limiting whitening-bias training to the first 20% of steps. LS 0.09, SiLU, jitter and LR-to-0 were already refuted here (E009/E037, E003, E008, E015).

findings.claim: The fast.ai/DIUx 18-minute ImageNet run combined progressive resizing (128 -> 224 -> 288) with a larger batch size during the low-res phase and smaller batches for the expensive high-res fine-tuning (dynamic batch sizes).
findings.relevance: Supports a direction the tree has not tested: a per-phase batch size, e.g. bs 2048-3072 at 16/24 px and 1024-1536 at 32 px. E038 showed fewer steps saved ~2 ms/step, more than Muon's ~1 ms, because per-step costs are a larger share in the small-map 16/24 px phases. E022 showed Muon tolerates bs 2000 (-0.25 pp). The large-batch phase would then cover only the cheap epochs, while the binding 32 px tail (E025) keeps more updates.

findings.claim: Merrill et al. (NeurIPS 2025), on OLMo: the critical batch size is near 0 at initialization, rises quickly and then plateaus. Batch-size warmup (start small, double as the critical batch size grows) trained 1B models with 43% fewer gradient steps without loss degradation.
findings.relevance: Caveat for the per-phase batch idea: theory and LM evidence say large batches hurt most at the start of training, which is exactly the 16 px phase. If the cheap phase gets a larger batch, a short small-batch start (or bs ramping up within the low-res phase) may avoid the penalty. Expect the accuracy cost of bs 3072 at 16 px to exceed the -0.25 pp E022 measured for a uniform bs 2000.

findings.claim: An agent-driven research loop cut CIFAR-10 airbench96 wall-clock by 4.59% (26.36 -> 25.15 s) at the 96% gate. It removed validation overhead, shortened the schedule and raised LR intensity. Its final near-miss (trial 060, below the accuracy gate) became feasible through a 'warmup repair' (retuned LR warmup). 81 of 97 trials failed the gate.
findings.relevance: LR warmup length/shape has not been tested in the tree; LS, the LR floor, and Muon lr/momentum have. Our step count changed (bs 1536, ~256 steps) while the warmup was only rescaled. Warmup is a zero-cost accuracy lever that recovered a near-miss in a similar airbench setting, so it could buy the ~0.2-0.3 pp that E040/E041-type cuts need.

findings.claim: Fable's CIFAR-10 record (1.828 s vs 1.978 s hiverge): 28->32 curriculum -0.128 s, deepening to 24->28->32 a further -0.081 s. Global max pooling (x.flatten(2).max(2)) was needed at 24 px (2x2 maps). A single CUDA graph over the whole ~284-step run with foreach-fused optimizer steps gave only ~5 ms over per-step graphs. Under fair measurement, the systems work as a whole was ~0.04 s slower than plain torch.compile. Excluded exploits: thermal cooldown ~9 ms, host lottery, moving work off the clock.
findings.relevance: Independent confirmation of the E004/E010/E011 energy-bound model: graph/fusion work is near-neutral. Fable kept its cheap phase at >=24 px; our 16 px finding (E026) goes beyond it. Reinforces that the launch-bound portion is small except for Muon.

findings.claim: Turbo-Muon AOL preconditioning (X0 * diag(rowsum|X0^T X0|)^-1/2 instead of Frobenius normalization) allows removing one NS iteration out of 5 in LM settings. On the CIFAR-10 speedrun it gave 94.03% in 1.348 s vs Muon+ 94.04% in 1.359 s, only -0.8% runtime.
findings.relevance: Weak support for H7.2.2-style NS savings. The CIFAR gain is <1%, and E031 showed dropping from 3 to 2 iterations costs 1.8 pp. AOL could make 2 iterations behave like 3, but the expected payoff is ~0.3 ms/step (~2%) at best, with real risk; E033's spectra suggest testing it offline on captured gradients first.

findings.claim: Drop-Muon updates only a randomly sampled suffix of layers per step (truncated backprop, probability shifting from shallow to deep layers). It reports up to 1.4x wall-clock on MNIST. On CIFAR-10 (3-layer CNN, 128/256/512 channels) gains were modest, reported only as reaching 90% training accuracy earlier.
findings.relevance: A possible new lever: skip backward through group 1 (the most expensive full-res layer) on some 32 px steps. Evidence for test accuracy on CIFAR is weak.

findings.claim: FreezeOut (progressively freezing early layers and excluding them from backprop) gave ~20% wall-clock savings without accuracy loss for ResNets on CIFAR, ~3% accuracy loss for DenseNets, and no improvement for VGG networks.
findings.relevance: Our net is VGG-like (3-conv groups, no residuals), the case where FreezeOut gave no benefit. This is evidence against freezing whitening/group 1 during the 32 px tail as a time lever.

findings.claim: A critical-damping momentum schedule mu(t)=1-2*sqrt(alpha(t)) reaches 90% on CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 2.34x faster but ends 0.46 pp lower. The hybrid (switch to mu=0.9 later) recovers final accuracy. On CIFAR-100 the accuracy cost grows to -1.7 pp.
findings.relevance: Evidence against momentum scheduling as an accuracy lever on CIFAR-100. Consistent with E027/E030: Muon momentum is flat in 0.5-0.6 and steep above.

findings.claim: NorMuon adds per-neuron (row-wise) second-moment normalization after Muon's orthogonalization. It reports 11.31% better training efficiency than Muon at 1.1B LM pretraining with similar memory. No CNN/CIFAR results.
findings.relevance: A possible per-update quality lever under H7 (Muon is the binding constraint). The extra cost is one row-norm EMA per step, which fuses cheaply, but there is no vision evidence and gains at ~250 steps are unknown.

findings.claim: MUD replaces Muon's Newton-Schulz polar step with a triangular (Cholesky-like) whitening surrogate. It reports 10-50% wall-clock gains over Muon/AdamW and 1.3-2.6x tokens/s on transformers (A100). No CNN results.
findings.relevance: An alternative way to cut Muon's remaining fixed per-step cost (~1 ms/step). Untested on convs; E031 shows orthogonalization quality is accuracy-critical here, so this is high risk.

findings.claim: The benchmark's official baseline is a ResNet9-style net, 40 epochs, width 64, on an A100 80GB PCIe: 75.36% mean accuracy (2 trials: 75.56%, 75.16%) at 59.30 s prepare+train; eval 0.117 s. On an L40 over 50 trials: 75.48% at 62.3 s. No other leaderboard entries are published.
findings.relevance: No public CIFAR-100 recipe beats the loop's 5.2 s; the best public one is futurebiohackers at 8.11 s. The L40's 50-trial mean shows a cross-seed sd that makes the 40-seed official mean tight, consistent with H4's margin rule.
